ancient.label: Pre-modern usage
ancient.about: Metals and minerals known long before modern chemistry kept their old names: the Five Metals 金 銀 銅 鐵 錫 (五金), plus 鉛, 汞, 硫, 硼 and 炭.

hobson1849.label: Tiānwén Lüèlùn
hobson1849.about: The first Chinese names for oxygen (養氣, nourishing gas) and nitrogen (淡氣, diluting gas), in a digest of astronomy by the medical missionary Benjamin Hobson.

hobson1855.label: Bówù Xīnbiān
hobson1855.about: Hobson’s natural philosophy treatise, printed at the London Missionary Society press in Shanghai. It mentions 56 elements (元質) and names hydrogen 輕氣, light gas; names were not yet consistent.

martin1868.label: Géwù Rùmén
martin1868.who: W. A. P. Martin (丁韙良), Tongwen College
martin1868.about: The first Chinese chemistry textbook, volume six of Martin’s Tongwen College course. Twenty-five elements get Chinese names, mostly two-character glosses by property: 灰精 essence of ash for potassium, 玻精 essence of glass for silicon. Only three names are single characters.

kerr1870.label: Huàxué Chūjiē
kerr1870.who: John G. Kerr (嘉約翰) & Hé Liǎorán (何瞭然)
kerr1870.about: A medical chemistry text from the Canton Hospital, based on Fownes and Wells. It moved to one-character names, coining new characters freely, and adopted Fryer’s principles after correspondence in 1869.

macgowan1871.label: Jīnshí Shíbié
macgowan1871.who: D. J. MacGowan (瑪高溫) & Huà Héngfāng (華蘅芳)
macgowan1871.about: A translation of Dana’s Manual of Mineralogy. Its atomic-weight table renders names as multi-character transliterations: 素地恩 sodium, 夕里西恩 silicium.

xu1871.label: Huàxué Jiànyuán
xu1871.who: Xú Shòu (徐壽) & John Fryer (傅蘭雅), Jiangnan Arsenal
xu1871.about: The most influential chemistry text of nineteenth-century China, translated from Wells at the Jiangnan Arsenal. Section 29 sets out the rule still in force: take the first syllable of the Western name, write it with one character, and add a radical for the class. Of its 64 names, 41 to 44 survive today.

billequin1873.label: Huàxué Zhǐnán
billequin1873.who: Anatole Billequin (畢利幹) & Lián Zǐzhèn (聯子振)
billequin1873.about: Billequin at Tongwen College rejected transliteration, fearing dialect differences, and named by property instead: 生色 colour-generating for chromium, 錆 for cobalt after its blue salts. The system did not spread.

ea1898.label: Revised List of Chemical Elements
ea1898.who: Educational Association of China (益智書會)
ea1898.about: The Educational Association’s attempt to unify the competing systems, agreed with the China Medical Missionary Association. Coined 氜 for helium.

du1900.label: Yàquán Zázhì
du1900.about: The first Chinese-run science journal. Dù Yàquán introduced the 气 radical for gases with 氬 argon and proposed 鈹, 鐠, 鐿, 銩 and 釓, all still in use.

ea1901.label: Chemical Terms and Nomenclature
ea1901.who: Educational Association of China (益智書會)
ea1901.about: The Association’s nomenclature for compounds, whose element list wrote some gases as 气 over a full character (气+養, 气+綠) and used 銤 for osmium and 釦 for cobalt.

du1905.label: Huàxué Xīn Jiàokēshū
du1905.about: Dù Yàquán’s textbook after Yoshida Hikoroku. Its periodic table records the characters in use in 1905, several of which were later reassigned: 鍶 then meant scandium, 錯 cerium, 銤 osmium.

moe1915.label: Draft inorganic nomenclature
moe1915.who: Ministry of Education, Republic of China
moe1915.about: A draft that adopted 氦 for helium.

moe1933.label: Principles of Chemical Nomenclature
moe1933.who: Zhèng Zhènwén (鄭貞文), National Institute for Compilation and Translation
moe1933.about: Drafted by Zhèng Zhènwén and ratified at Nanjing, this fixed the modern system: every element one character, 氫 氧 氮 氯 for the gases, 矽 for silicon. Later elements follow its rules.

moe1945.label: Principles of Chemical Nomenclature, revised
moe1945.who: Ministry of Education, Republic of China
moe1945.about: Minor revision: 氡 for radon, 鈮 replacing columbium 鈳, 釓 for gadolinium.

prc1951.label: Principles of Chemical Nomenclature, PRC revision
prc1951.who: Academia Sinica / Ministry of Education, PRC
prc1951.about: Mainland revision adding the first transuranic elements 鎿 鈈 鎇 錇 鐦.

prc1955.label: Inorganic terms review
prc1955.about: Changed 矽 to 硅 and 鎦 to 鑥 to remove homophones with 硒/錫 and 硫.

prc1980.label: Principles of Inorganic Nomenclature
prc1980.about: Used the pre-1997 American names for 104 and 105, hence a character for hahnium.

xinhua1980.label: Xīnhuá Cídiǎn
xinhua1980.about: Dictionary entry recording 鎷 for masurium, the disputed 1925 claim to element 43.

prc1991.label: Chemical Terms
prc1991.who: China National Committee for Terms in Sciences and Technologies (全國科學技術名詞審定委員會)
prc1991.about: The first standard of the national terms committee; finalised 鍀, 鉕, 砹, 鈁 and unified all 109 elements known then.

prc1998.label: Names of elements 101–109
prc1998.about: Chinese names for 101–109 after IUPAC settled the transfermium wars in 1997.

prc2003.label: Name of element 110
prc2003.about: 鐽 for darmstadtium, reusing an old tantalum character.

prc2007.label: Name of element 111
prc2007.about: 錀 for roentgenium, agreed in 2006 and published in 2007.

prc2012.label: Name of element 112
prc2012.about: 鎶 for copernicium, reusing the old columbium character.

prc2013.label: Names of elements 114 and 116
prc2013.about: New characters for flerovium and livermorium.

prc2017.label: Names of elements 113, 115, 117, 118
prc2017.who: CNCTST with the State Language Commission
prc2017.about: 鉨 鏌 鿬 鿫 for the four elements named by IUPAC in 2016, chosen in a public review with the State Language Commission.

tw2010.label: Name of element 112, Taiwan
tw2010.zh: 國立編譯館化學名詞審議委員會
tw2010.who: National Institute for Compilation and Translation, Taiwan
tw2010.about: Taiwan adopted 鎶 for copernicium two years before the mainland.

tw2012.label: Names of elements 114 and 116, Taiwan (provisional)
tw2012.zh: 國家教育研究院化學名詞審譯委員會
tw2012.who: National Academy for Educational Research, Taiwan

tw.label: Current Taiwan standard
tw.zh: 臺灣正體（國家教育研究院）
tw.who: National Academy for Educational Research, Taiwan
tw.about: Where Taiwan’s standard differs from the mainland: 矽, 鎝, 鎦, 砈, 鍅, 錼, 鈽, 鋂, 鉳, 鉲, 鑀, and different readings for 鈹, 銻, 鋦.

proposal.label: Proposed, not adopted
proposal.about: Characters proposed or used informally but never standardised.

bloc.label: Eastern-bloc usage
bloc.about: Names used in Soviet-aligned textbooks during the transfermium disputes.

japanese.label: Japanese-mediated transliteration
japanese.about: Transliterations that reached Chinese through Japanese.
